label: Note Input
title: Note Input
summary: Use a Note Input for a short, optional memo under an amount, such as “Rent for April”, that grows as people type.
corePrinciple: An optional memo that stays out of the way until tapped.

anatomy.title: A grey pill around the note
anatomy.description: The pill hugs its text: the placeholder until people type, then the note itself. Tapping anywhere on it starts typing, and a long note wraps inside it.
blocks: Light grey with round ends; tap anywhere on it to type.
14 px bold; the placeholder looks the same.

configuration.title: A placeholder, then the note
configuration.description: Note Input has no variants. Set the placeholder to say what the note is for. The note keeps what people type, and the screen reads it to send with the payment.

sizing.title: 35 px tall, as wide as its text
sizing.description: The pill is 35 px tall for one line, with 8 px above and below the text and 16 px at each end. Its width follows the text up to the width of its container; a longer note wraps onto more lines.

content.title: A few words people will recognise later
content.description: The note travels with the payment, so keep it to a few words about what the money is for. Use the placeholder for a hint, not an instruction.

inContext.title: A memo under the transfer amount
inContext.description: Amount Input places the note under the amount. The screen keeps both values and sends the note with the payment.

sources.title: Use the public Note Input contract
sources.description: The guide compares the Figma component with the installed package and its Storybook stories.
blocks: Installed jfs-components is 0.1.78 (12 October build) from the team’s private package repository. Figma’s Note Input has Idle and Editing variants, 95 × 34; the package has none: it follows focus, grows with the text, wraps a long note inside the pill, and is 35 px tall for one line. Its colours are the same in Dark mode, so this page shows Light only. It keeps what people type on its own, or takes its value from the screen. On the web each note is one Tab stop, its text is read once, and it keeps its name, the placeholder or yours, while focused. A read-only note is faded and can’t be focused. Enter starts a new line in the note. The published Storybook has one story; newer stories are not deployed yet.
